newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia approves oil reserves list in final vote.
newsitem.headline: Russia approves oil reserves list in final vote.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament gave final approval on Tuesday to a list of seven energy and mineral deposits eligible for development under production-sharing deals.

But the approval is only a small victory for foreign energy investors, who want a comprehensive list of the reserves open to investment rather than a piece-meal approach parcelling out natural resource deposits over time.
The reserves list bill now goes to the upper house, the Federation Council, and then to President Boris Yeltsin.

Two hundred and forty six deputies approved the list while 109 voted against it. Three officials abstained from voting during the session, officially the Duma's last working day before its summer recess.
The Duma has said it will approve deposits gradually and present separate bills in the future itemising more reserves open to production-sharing deals.
Under the bill approved on Tuesday, foreign investors may participate in developing only two deposits, the Kuranakh gold group and the Prirazlomnoye oil deposit on the Barent's Sea shelf.

The other five deposits, open only to domestic investors, are the giant Samotlor oil and gas condensate field, the Krasnoleninskoye oil deposit, the Yakovlevskoye iron ore deposit, the Romanshkinskoye oil field and oil deposits near Russia's Far Eastern island of Sakhalin.

Russia has a production-sharing law, but U.S., Japanese, European and other oil companies are waiting for Moscow to approve reserves open to output-sharing deals before proceeding with tens of billions of dollars in planned investments.
The original reserves list listed over 200 deposits but was cut after conservative politicians said Moscow could end up the loser if it opened its natural resources to outside investment.
